fixed_before: holdout v2 student and sentence selection, annotation, and any holdout v2 prediction

data.excluded_students: the 25 students of cell_reliability_holdout_v1, opened on 2026-11-06; selection runs on the 73 remaining holdout students
data.selection: the same CELL pilot procedure (src/cell_pilot.py) as holdout v1: structural metadata for students, parser-derived structural categories for sentences; no labels, verdicts, predictions, quality, length, or duplicate flags
data.reserve: the other 37 holdout students stay untouched for a later evaluation

parse.pipeline: frozen en_core_web_sm 3.8.0 with spaCy 3.8.13 (sentence segmentation v1)
parse.context: each sentence is a span of its complete essay parse

annotation.labeller: a new separate model session (annotator_id claude_sealed_holdout_v2) that sees only a blind packet: sentence, neighbouring sentences, token parse, clause heads, and the annotation guideline
labeller_must_not_see: Syntax Reliability verdicts or flags of any version
Reliability ML features, probabilities, or predictions
development results, error analyses, holdout v1 results, and project history
annotation.owner_review: the dataset owner reviews every UNRELIABLE, MOSTLY_RELIABLE, and NOT_ANALYZABLE label and a seeded random sample of 40 RELIABLE labels (seed 20261106); reviewed records become adjudicated by human_owner_v1
annotation.freeze: labels are locked by file hash before the evaluation run; no label changes after the run

systems.reference: Syntax Reliability v1.2 warning (medium or low)
systems.primary_candidate: Syntax Reliability v1.4 warning (medium or low), compared with v1.3 to isolate the segmentation_boundary_conflict signal
secondary_candidates: Syntax Reliability v1.3 and v1.4 warnings, each compared with v1.2
Reliability ML Model B, refit on all 606 development observations with the threshold chosen by the heuristic_precision rule exactly as in holdout v1 (expected 0.9238), compared with v1.2
not_evaluated: Clause Detection v2.2 and sentence segmentation v2, whose labels would need re-judging

analysis.analysis_set: labelled analyzable sentences where v1.2 does not abstain; abstentions are counted and reported separately
metrics: true and false positive and negative counts
analysis.paired_comparison: discordant counts on UNRELIABLE sentences (recall) and on usable sentences (false warnings), each with a two-sided exact McNemar test, for v1.4 against v1.3 and for v1.3, v1.4, and Model B against v1.2
analysis.primary_question: Does the v1.4 segmentation warning raise recall over v1.3 without adding false warnings?
analysis.decision_rule: the v1.4 signal is confirmed if its recall gain over v1.3 on UNRELIABLE sentences is significant (exact McNemar p < 0.05) and it adds no significant false warnings; if v1.4 adds significant false warnings or loses catches, the result is negative and analyze_writing returns to v1.3; otherwise the result is inconclusive and v1.4 stays the default as a development candidate
analysis.power_note: on development data the signal fired on 10 of 652 sentences (6 UNRELIABLE, 3 NOT_ANALYZABLE, none usable); holdout v1 had 13 UNRELIABLE sentences with a segmentation failure among 277, so about 15 to 20 are expected here and a significant result needs most of them caught by the signal
analysis.no_pooling: holdout v1 and v2 are reported separately; holdout v1 students were opened before v1.4 existed and are not re-scored as untouched data

opening_procedure: freeze this plan, the evaluated code, and the development set lock in git
prepare the batch, write the blind packet, and label it in a new sealed session; owner review follows in that session
lock the holdout v2 labels by hash
record the opening in split_v1.json (holdout_openings) and in PROJECT_HISTORY.md
run the evaluation once and report every planned number, whatever the outcome
after opening, the 36 evaluated students are no longer untouched; the 37 remaining holdout students are the only untouched data left
